hypotheses.title: At 160 modules with twelve act rounds each, waiting for the trace reaches zero failing checks in fewer waves than a manager
At 160 modules with twelve act rounds each, waiting for the trace ends with fewer failing checks than a manager
At 160 modules with twelve act rounds each, waiting for the trace leaves fewer checks failing on fresh inputs than a manager
At 160 modules with twelve act rounds each, waiting for the trace uses fewer output tokens per case than a manager

bench.reportNote: 160 modules is not a new size: it is the largest size already tested in LI26, LI27 and LI33. What changes from those studies is LI36's directed-edge density (320 directed and 80 symmetric edges) and the 12 act rounds per arm.
